caption: NOT gate with a lever input (track gates): the lever strongly powers the stone it hangs on; a torch on top of that stone inverts it. 2 gt.
OR gate with lever inputs (track gates): both levers hang on one stone and strongly power it; the output cell above the stone sees it. 0 gt, one block.
NOR gate with lever inputs (track gates): both levers hang on the same stone and strongly power it; a torch on top of the stone is lit only when neither lever is on. 2 gt.

OR gate, instant (track gates): one dust on a stone between the two inputs; either input powers the dust, the dust powers the stone under it, and the output cell under the stone sees it. 0 gt. (With the output cell itself between the inputs the OR needs no block at all.)
NOR with real signal inputs: one dust between the two inputs (either input powers it, that is OR), on a stone whose wall torch is lit only when the dust is off. 2 gt, 3 blocks.

AND with real signal inputs: a torch stands on each input block, so each goes out when its input turns on; the dust between them is then off exactly when both inputs are on, and the wall torch hanging under that dust turns it back into AND. 4 gt, 5 blocks.

XOR gate, 21 blocks, 2 ticks: two subtract comparators, each with one input behind it and the other at its side, so each lights only when its own input is on alone. The trick is the side feeds: a dust lying ON input A's block reaches the upper comparator's side, and a dust UNDER input B's block reaches the lower one's, each at full strength because it touches the powered input block itself, so the two inputs cross in height instead of around each other. The lower comparator lights the lamp directly; the upper one powers a block whose dust climbs over the core and lands on the lamp. A stone above A's dust keeps that dust from joining the route over the top.

XNOR gate, 23 blocks, 4 ticks: the 21-block XOR (two subtract comparators, each input crossing to the other comparator's side through a dust lying on or under its own block) whose two signals meet on a stone instead of the lamp; a wall torch on that stone is the output, lit unless exactly one input is on.

NOT gate, 1 block: a wall torch hanging on the input block itself. The input powers that block, the torch goes out, and the torch is the output: lit exactly when the input is off. A row of them side by side inverts a whole bus.

NAND gate, 2 blocks: a wall torch hanging on each input block, and the output lamp touching both torches. Each torch goes out when its own input is on, so the lamp stays lit unless BOTH inputs are on.

IMPLY gate (A implies B), 3 blocks, glitch-free: the output lamp touches a wall torch hanging on input A (lit while A is off) and the repeater that input B arrives on. The repeater gives B the same 2 ticks the torch takes, so switching both inputs at once never blinks the lamp.

IMPLY gate (B implies A), 3 blocks, glitch-free: the mirror of gate-imply. The output lamp touches a wall torch hanging on input B (lit while B is off) and the repeater that input A arrives on; the repeater gives A the same 2 ticks the torch takes, so switching both inputs at once never blinks the lamp.

NIMPLY gate (A and not B), 4 blocks: a subtract comparator reads input A's block behind it and, at its side, a dust lying against input B's block; it passes A minus B, so the output lights only while A is on and B is off.

NIMPLY gate (B and not A), 4 blocks: the mirror of gate-nimply. A subtract comparator reads input B's block behind it and, at its side, a dust lying against input A's block; the output lights only while B is on and A is off.
